# Starter AGENTS.md

AGENTS.md is one page you ask any AI tool to read first when it opens your AI-Labs folder. Claude writes yours in Lab 1 by interviewing you, which takes about ten minutes. This file holds the interview prompt that starts it.

## Before Lab 1: save this file

Save this file in `AI-Labs` (prompt 2 in the Lab 1 kit moves it into `Kits`) and keep its name, `STARTER-AGENTS.md`. Don't rename it to AGENTS.md. Claude writes that file separately, and two files with the same name would confuse the check at the end.

If you didn't save it, you can still run the interview. Copy the prompt from this page.

## Start the interview

1. Open your folder.
   - Desktop app: start a Cowork session on the `AI-Labs` folder itself, not a folder inside it.
   - Browser: open your AI-Labs Project and start a new chat inside it.
2. Copy the prompt under "The interview prompt" below and paste it into Claude. It's one long paragraph, and triple-clicking it selects all of it.
   - In Cowork, if this file is in `Kits`, you can type this instead: `Read Kits/STARTER-AGENTS.md and run the interview prompt in it.`
3. Answer one question at a time. Say "done" when the six headings are covered.

## Save what Claude writes

- Desktop app: Claude saves `AGENTS.md` at the top of `AI-Labs`, next to `Kits` and `Working`. If it asks before saving, say yes. Check the file is there.
- Browser: if Claude gives you AGENTS.md as a file, download it into `AI-Labs`. If it shows the text instead, copy the text into a plain text file named `AGENTS.md` and save it in `AI-Labs`.
  - Windows Notepad: choose "Save as type: All files" and type AGENTS.md as the name.
  - Mac TextEdit: choose Format, then Make Plain Text, before you save.

  Then upload `AGENTS.md` to your Project.

## Check it works

Start fresh: in the desktop app, a new Cowork session on `AI-Labs` itself; in the browser, a new chat inside your AI-Labs Project. Paste:

```
Read AGENTS.md first. What did I ask you to follow in this folder? Name the three rules that matter most.
```

If Claude can't find `AGENTS.md`, check you opened `AI-Labs` itself (in the browser, the AI-Labs Project). If it names rules you didn't mean, fix them in `AGENTS.md` in Notepad or TextEdit, then start fresh and ask again. In the browser, remove the old copy from your Project and upload the fixed one first.

## The interview prompt

```
I'm setting up a workspace folder for my organization's AI work, and I'd like you to interview me so we can write its instruction file, AGENTS.md. Ask me one question at a time and wait for my answer before asking the next. Cover these six headings: Who we are; Who we write for; How we sound; What never goes in this folder or any AI tool; Where things live in this folder; What "done" means for our work. When an answer is vague, ask me for an example. If you can see the folder, describe where things live yourself and check it with me. Stop after about ten questions, or sooner if I say "done." Then write the file under those six headings in plain language, one page at most, using my words where you can. Don't add anything I didn't tell you, with one exception: start the "What never goes in" heading with this rule, word for word: "Clients, donors, volunteers and anyone we serve never go into AI tools or this folder, and neither do health or case details. Staff names in our everyday writing are fine." Never write a real person's name, story, health detail or a confidential address into this file, even under "What never goes in." If I give you one, leave it out and tell me. If a heading is still thin, write "To fill in" under it. If you can save files in this folder, save it as AGENTS.md at the top level; if you can't, show me the full text so I can copy it.
```

## What the finished file looks like

Claude fills this in for you, so there's nothing to type here. The line under each heading says what goes there.

```
# (Your organization's name) AI workspace

## Who we are
What we do, where, and for whom, in two or three sentences.

## Who we write for
The people who read what we send: board, funders, volunteers, families, partners.

## How we sound
Our writing at its best, with one or two sentences we'd actually write.

## What never goes in this folder or any AI tool
Clients, donors, volunteers and anyone we serve never go into AI tools or this folder, and neither do health or case details. Staff names in our everyday writing are fine. Then our organization's own rules.

## Where things live in this folder
What each folder holds: Kits, Working, Recipes, Outputs, and any added later.

## What "done" means for our work
How we know a piece is ready to send, and who checks it before it goes.
```
